title: P-3: both gateways register in one process — routes.js becomes a barrel, routes-live-animals.js gains the set-context wiring, co-residency.test.js is born
recipe: SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §4.1 / §4.4 / §4.5 + §5 P-3, all as REVISED 2026-08-01 by ruling R3 (co-residency). FD-1/FD-2 are REVISED: there is no served-set env var and routes.js is a BARREL, not a selector. No recipe doc exists yet (docs/add-a-set.md is pp-053, which lands after this increment and describes the shape this increment creates) — the plan sections are the script.

filesToTouch.what: The current src/server/app/routes.js body (lines 1-77) MOVED here, then given the co-residency wiring. It sits in the same directory so every relative './…' specifier resolves unchanged. Still exports `liveAnimals`; plugin name stays 'live-animals'. Changes to the register body, in the LOAD-BEARING order of §4.4.3 (context → mount → config → assertions → dispatch → persistence → cookies → guard → priming → routes): (0) call `registerSetMount('live-animals', '')` and install the realm-scoped context extension `server.ext('onPreAuth', (request, h) => { enterSetContext('live-animals'); return h.continue })` as the FIRST things in the body, and wrap the WHOLE remainder in `await withSetContext('live-animals', async () => { … })` so the boot-time reads (assertObligationPurity, assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage, buildDispatch) resolve this set; (1-9) add `'live-animals'` as the FIRST argument to every configure*/build* call that pp-056 keyed — configureObligationSet, configureFulfilmentRegistry, configureCommodityReference, configureJourneyFlow, buildDispatch, configureRecords, configureSession; (10) `registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '', cookieNames: SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES })` replacing the bare registerJourneyCookie(server) — live-animals' base is '' so its cookie path stays '/'; (11) the existing onPreHandler entry-guard extension unchanged (already realm-scoped — the proven precedent for FD-15); (12) countries.prime()/ports.prime() unchanged and still guarded by isRealMode(). NO URL change, NO behavioural change. Import registerSetMount/enterSetContext/withSetContext from './shared/set-context.js'. Do not add migration comments — git history is the record.

Full rewrite as a BARREL (FD-2 as revised). At this increment it is one line: `export { liveAnimals } from './routes-live-animals.js'`. pp-007 adds the second line `export { plantProducts } from './routes-plant-products.js'` when that file exists. There is NO selector, NO SETS map, NO servedSet()/servedSetName(), and NO read of process.env anywhere in this file — a served-set env var is exactly what ruling R3 deleted. routes.js keeps its dep-cruiser routes-is-the-gateway allowlist entry even though a barrel no longer imports sets/** directly (removing it would be an unrelated semantic change — P-4/pp-010).

Line 7 import stays `import { liveAnimals } from './app/routes.js'` (the barrel now supplies it); lines ~20/26 keep `const routes = [liveAnimals]`, the authEnabled signout push, and `await server.register(routes)` exactly as today — live-animals' registration is byte-equivalent in effect, which is the point. The SECOND registration — `await server.register(plantProducts, { routes: { prefix: '/plant-products' } })` as a SEPARATE register call, because the prefix option applies to a whole call — is added by pp-007, which is the increment that creates the plant gateway. Touch nothing else in router.js. If the diff here is empty, say so in the increment log rather than inventing a change.

Minimal slice of P-4 pulled forward because this increment's own ladder runs lint:arch and routes-live-animals.js imports sets/live-animals/**. `routes-is-the-gateway` rule (line 31): the `from.pathNot` array (currently exactly [`^${APP}/sets/`, `^${APP}/routes\\.js$`, '\\.test\\.js$']) gains `` `^${APP}/routes-live-animals\\.js$` ``. Do NOT regenerate .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json (baseline discipline).

THE standing co-residency evidence file (T-9). Created here with the LIVE-ANIMALS HALF ONLY; pp-007 adds the plant half, and every later platform increment extends it when it adds a seam. It must never be folded into another file — it is the one test that can fail for 'co-residency broke' and nothing else. At this increment it boots ONE @hapi/hapi server, registers `liveAnimals` through the new shape, and asserts: (a) GET '/' returns 200 with live-animals dashboard content; (b) the request resolved the live-animals set — assert through observable behaviour, e.g. a page whose rendering depends on the live-animals manifest/journey flow, plus the liveAnimals* cookie names on the response; (c) REALM-SCOPING PIN (§4.1 risk 1, load-bearing) — register a second trivial plugin owning a route OUTSIDE the live-animals realm and prove the live-animals onPreHandler entry guard does NOT run for it, which is the mechanism pp-007's cross-set version depends on; (d) ALS-INTERLEAVING PIN (§4.1 risk 2) — two concurrent injections, the first deliberately awaiting inside its handler, both still resolving their own set context (at this increment both are live-animals, so the pin is structural; pp-007 upgrades it to a genuine cross-set pair); (e) the four accessors from pp-005 read the live-animals policy under this context. Structure the file so pp-007 adds cases rather than rewrites it: a shared `bootServer({ sets })` helper taking the gateways to register.

The existing 'promoted live-animals route authentication' describe imports allRoutes from the set directly and is unaffected by the barrel — leave it untouched. DELETE nothing else and ADD no selector tests: there is no selector, no SERVED_SET and no unknown-set error to pin (the round-1 plan of this increment specified exactly those three cases; ruling R3 removes them). If a `grep -rn 'SERVED_SET'` in this file finds anything, it is a leftover and must go.

notes: AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency) — RETITLED AND RESCOPED, which is a genuine scope change, not a wording tidy. The round-1 increment built a boot-time SERVED_SET selector: routes.js held a SETS map, servedSetName()/servedSet() read process.env lazily, router.js registered [servedSet()], and routes.test.js pinned three selector cases including an unknown-value throw. ALL of that is deleted by the reversal. There is no selector, no SETS map, no env var and no unknown-set error. routes.js becomes a two-line barrel (one line until pp-007 lands the plant gateway); the real gateway is routes-live-animals.js, which gains the set-context wiring; and the process serves both sets simultaneously rather than choosing one. NEW DEPENDENCIES: pp-056 (P-9 — the seams must be keyed by set before two sets can register) and pp-057 (P-10 — URLs must be namespaced before two sets can both claim /notifications/…). ID CONVENTION for the reversal's four new increments: pp-056 = P-9 set-context module + per-set seam keying; pp-057 = P-10 per-set URL namespace; pp-058 = P-11 setId-first tripwire; pp-053 = G-A/R6 docs/add-a-set.md. PHASING DECISION (headless — the plan's §4.4 end-state vs §9's ordering): §4.4 describes the finished shape (barrel exports both, router registers both), but §9 puts P-3 in phase m0-a with live-animals as the only set and the plant gateway in m0-b. Importing or registering a routes-plant-products.js that does not exist is impossible and a stub placeholder would be dead code, so this increment lands the live-animals half of the end-state and pp-007 adds the barrel's second export plus router.js's separate prefixed register call. Both halves are named in pp-007's filesToTouch so nothing is orphaned. The same split applies to co-residency.test.js: born here with the live-animals half and a bootServer({ sets }) seam, completed by pp-007. TWO RISKS THIS INCREMENT MUST RETIRE, NOT ASSUME (§4.1): realm scoping is real (Hapi scopes request-lifecycle extensions added inside a plugin to that plugin's routes — the live-animals entry guard is ALREADY a realm-scoped onPreHandler at routes.js:65-68, so the mechanism is proven in this codebase and onPreAuth simply runs earlier in the same lifecycle), and enterWith survives interleaving. Both get pins here in structural form and cross-set form at pp-007; a red interleaving pin is a STOP-and-replan, not a patch. Also handed over from pp-005: co-residency.test.js gains the assertion that the two sets read DIFFERENT enforcedAtContinue values in one process — the case lands with the plant half at pp-007, and pp-005 already proves the same divergence at unit level. Two-sided verification rule (REVISED, R3): 'both sets serve correctly from the SAME running process' is the standing bar, but it cannot be fully exercised until pp-007 registers the second gateway; the bar HERE is that live-animals is provably unchanged (byte-identical URLs, no spec edits, no env vars) and that the co-residency mechanism itself is pinned. Exemplar files to read before writing: src/server/app/routes.js:1-77 (the body being moved, incl. the 13 wiring calls at 47-73 and the entry-guard ext at 65-68), src/server/router.js:7,20,26, .dependency-cruiser.cjs:25-34, src/server/app/routes.test.js:1-13, and pp-056's shared/set-context.js as landed.
